sites.function: _compute_poi_activation_history — enter transition
sites.question: From which candle does this same-direction imbalance count toward cond3 ("an unfilled same-direction imbalance exists after the IC as of t")?
sites.window: relevant instances (:912-918) are unfilled on [enter_idx, confirmed_fill_idx-1], clipped to [first_active, scan_end]
sites.check_to_idx: Implicit: the sweep candle t. enter_idx = max(inst.start_idx, first_active) adds the instance to the unfilled set at its c2. This matches the cond3 formula in the comment at :516-518, has_unfilled_imbalance(df, ic_idx+1, t, check_to_idx=t, direction=sd). For inst.end_idx >= t, is_filled returns False on an empty scan (common/types.py:194).
sites.as_of_explanation: t runs over [first_active, scan_end]. first_active = max(the cycle's CTS-established moment, ic_idx, the structure or sub floor) (:839-841). Every t is a real-time candle at which the POI's state is asserted.
sites.unknowable_reachable: Yes, whenever inst.start_idx >= first_active: the instance enters at its c2, before c3 = start_idx+1 has closed. Verified cases: H1 sid1 cyc2 IC 865 and IC 860 re-activate at 953 (single-candle instance 953) and at 997 (instance 997-999). M15 sub7 cyc0 IC 4048 re-activates at 4118 in both lenses, the c2 of the 2-candle instance (4118,4119). I ran the unmodified function on inputs rebuilt from the baseline save and it reproduces all 5 H1 CSV histories exactly.
sites.classification_rationale: The as-of is a real processing candle, and a live engine cannot see the instance at its c2: across every H1 and M15 instance, no instance is visible at t = start_idx. R1 is the exact live rule. From start_idx+1 the live prefix [start_idx, min(end_idx, t-1)] exists and is unfilled for every t in [start+1, end+1]: 385 H1 and 1464 M15 candle checks, 0 violations. The merged instance cannot be committed-filled before end+2 either. So entering at start+1 matches a live engine exactly, and R2 (end+1) is too late for merged runs.
sites.r1_vs_r2: R1 vs R2 matters here. R1 (enter at start+1) gives: H1 953->954 and 997->998 (confirmed_idx 997->998) on IC 865 and IC 860; M15 sub7 IC 4048 4118->4119. These are exactly last session's 4 measured rows. R2 (enter at end+1) gives 953->954 but 997->1000 (instance 997-999) and 4118->4120 (instance 4118-4119). R2 is wrong because a live engine sees the unfilled prefix from start+1. On single-candle instances R1 == R2 (953->954).
sites.effect_if_counted: The POI (re-)activates one candle early, at c2, when the entering instance is the only knowable unfilled same-direction instance. It can also hide a deactivation. Synthetic example: fixture _make_multicycle_data POI (0,2) IC 12 has history [(15,A)] today; under R1 it is [(15,A),(19,D)], because instance (14,14) commit-fills at 19 while (19..22) enters at its c2 19. The shift flows into activation_history, confirmed_idx (the last activate), current_versions/status, zone_proximity.py:487 (poi_active_as_of), and the chart's active stretches and confirm lines (export_m15_chart.py:1594-1634, 2506-2540; export_plotly). WVMI does not read activation_history. On the reference window: 4 POI rows.
sites.proposed_fix: enter_idx = max(inst.start_idx + 1, first_active) (R1). Better: add one named accessor on ImbalanceInstance for the first knowable candle (= start_idx + 1) and use it from the sweep and any wrapper. It is a moment, so it needs a name under the GLOSSARY Naming Standard (user's call; avoid clashing with the pool's knowable_at_idx). The :917 filter needs no change, because :921 already drops an instance whose enter candle passes scan_end. Update the docstring :817-819 ("enter unfilled set (inst.start_idx)"), the comment :924-925 ("[inst.start_idx, confirmed_fill_idx - 1]") and the cond3 comment :516-518. Add the c3 rule to IMBALANCE_FILL_SEMANTICS.md. Tests first: a direct _compute_poi_activation_history pin with an instance whose c2 == first_active, and the _make_multicycle_data (0,2) IC 12 full history.
tests_pinning: engine_v2/tests/test_poi_activation_moment.py:151-162 (pins only the first activation (15); the full history is deliberately unpinned (comment :157-159), and R1 adds (19,D))
No existing test pins entering at c2. I ran every test in test_poi_activation_moment in-process against an R1-patched sweep and all pass (the monkeypatch test was skipped as unrelated).

sites.function: _compute_poi_activation_history — the already-committed-filled skip and the leave transition
sites.question: Is the instance already committed-filled when it would enter? At which candle does it leave the unfilled set?
sites.check_to_idx: The cached confirmed_fill_idx (the stroke-2 candle) is compared with enter_idx (skip if confirmed <= enter). The leave transition is placed at confirmed_fill_idx when it is <= scan_end.
sites.as_of_explanation: confirmed_fill_idx is the close of the stroke-2 candle, a genuine moment. enter_idx is a processing candle.
sites.unknowable_reachable: It exists but cannot change anything. confirmed_fill_idx >= armed_idx >= end_idx+2, because the last c3 cannot arm its own gap. Bullish stroke 1 needs l[end+1] <= gap_top - 0.7*gap, but gap_top == l[end+1]; bearish mirrors this. Measured min(confirmed - end) = min(armed - end) = 2 over all 167 H1 and 622 M15 instances. So confirmed <= enter can only hold when enter == first_active > start+1, which is identical under the current rule, R1 and R2.
sites.classification_rationale: Neither the skip decision nor the leave candle depends on the enter rule (current, R1 or R2), and the leave is a real-time moment.
sites.r1_vs_r2: No difference: confirmed >= end+2 > end+1 >= start+1.
sites.effect_if_counted: None.
sites.proposed_fix: None. Optionally note in the comment that under the c3 rule the skip still triggers only through first_active.
tests_pinning: engine_v2/tests/test_imbalance.py:152-257 (two-stroke is_filled semantics; the cache mirrors them)
sites.call_frequency: Same as :920 (once per POI x relevant instance).

sites.as_of_explanation: scan_end = min(end_idx-1, last_candle) (:495) bounds the processing candles.
sites.unknowable_reachable: An instance with start_idx == scan_end passes the filter even though under R1 it can never enter; :921 (enter_idx > scan_end -> continue) drops it once enter uses start+1. sites.classification_rationale: The filter's output only matters through enter_idx, and :921 already enforces the scan_end bound for any enter rule.
sites.r1_vs_r2: No difference.

sites.window: (end_idx, end of df], one numpy scan per instance
sites.check_to_idx: None. The scan starts at _pos(inst.end_idx + 1) and runs to the end of df. The resulting moments are compared later against t (confirmed_fill_idx <= t is equivalent to is_filled(t)).
sites.as_of_explanation: It computes per-instance moments over the full df; the sweep consumes them causally by comparing with t.

That c3 cannot arm, as proved above; measured min(armed - end) = 2 on H1 and M15. A live engine tracking the growing prefix cannot arm on [start+1, end+1] either (verified). So armed_idx and confirmed_fill_idx are real-time moments.

sites.r1_vs_r2: The scan start is the R2 point by construction. Starting at the R1 point would be wrong: candles in (start, end] are c2s of the same run and would be tested against bounds that do not exist yet. It is also unnecessary, since nothing between R1 and R2 can arm.

sites.function: find_ic_candidates on the final/locked FibState (downstream POI derivation)
sites.question: Does this opposite-direction candle in the final fib's [BOS, CTS] span have a same-direction imbalance after it that is still unfilled, i.e. is it an IC candidate for the cycle?
sites.check_to_idx: fib_state.cts_idx (:204, :233): the fib's CTS point. For a locked fib this is the final CTS anchor; the lock moment (CTS_CONFIRMED) comes later. For an active, unlocked fib it is the latest CTS.
sites.as_of_explanation: cts_idx is used both as the window end (a location) and as the fill as-of (a time). The actual decision time is the lock moment or any t >= cts+1, which is always later than the anchor.
sites.unknowable_reachable: Yes, but only for instances with start_idx == cts_idx: overlap needs start <= cts, and unknowability needs start >= cts. Instances straddling the anchor (start < cts <= end) are R1-knowable and already give the right boolean. Measured: none of the 3 H1 fibs; no M15-confluence fib. M15-counter sub5 cyc1 (fib bos 3621, cts 3806; the never-established-cycle fallback fib) has instance (3806,3806,+1), and 39 candidates (3743..3805) qualify only through it. The variant pick is unchanged ({3654: V30,V60,V90}), so the POI delta is 0. An H1 in-memory run_pipeline with a c3 filter on this path gives identical POIs.
sites.classification_rationale: IC identification on the final fib is a retrospective location question, and the sweep enforces activation timing (cond3 re-evaluated per t; after the :920 fix only from c3). So an IC admitted through a c2-at-anchor instance cannot activate before that instance is knowable, unless another knowable unfilled instance justifies it, which a live engine would also accept. The as-of is the CTS anchor. At the real decision time (>= cts+1) the instance is knowable, so filtering c3 against the anchor would drop ICs a live engine qualifies at the lock moment: less faithful, although 0 delta on this window. Once Plan E splits cts_idx into a window end (anchor) and an as-of moment, start <= cts < moment makes this site already bounded and no c3 filter is needed.
sites.r1_vs_r2: R1 changes candidates only when start == cts (counter sub5 cyc1: 39 candidates, 0 POI delta). R2 would be wrong and gives different results: it drops straddling instances that a live engine sees. H1 fib (689,761) would lose candidates 753/755/757/758 (instance 760-761); M15 confluence sub0 cyc0 would lose 778/782 (instance 783-784); sub7 cyc2 would lose 4218/4220 (instance 4221-4222) in both lenses.
sites.effect_if_counted: It can admit extra IC candidates. That means a POI that would not otherwise exist, or a later IC displacing an earlier one in the most-recent-per-variant pick of select_ic_variants. This affects POI existence and versions, not activation timing. Reference window: 0.
sites.proposed_fix: No c3 change here. If the c3 rule goes inside has_unfilled_imbalance (the shared primitive), this call must opt out explicitly (an explicit knowability/as-of parameter), or it silently inherits the anchor-relative, less faithful behaviour. Record the c3 part as measured (0 delta) against PLAN_E_inputs §2.4 item 8 and its 'E3?' row.
tests_pinning: engine_v2/tests/test_imbalance.py:336-341 (has_unfilled_imbalance with check_to == window end; the instance is R1-knowable, so unaffected)

sites.call_frequency: Once per processed fib per derive_poi_zones call (:457): all non-disappeared fibs passing the :448 gate, for the H1 main and every sub projection. One has_unfilled_imbalance call per opposite-direction candle in [bos, cts].

sites.function: find_ic_candidates inside the MarketStructure in-flight resolver (poi_inners_resolver, wired at structure_engine.py:82)
sites.question: During the MarketStructure run: which IC inner prices exist for the current cycle's (possibly cross-cycle) fib? These feed the CTS confirmation by same-direction zone proximity.
sites.window: overlap with [idx+1, anchor_cts_idx]; anchor_cts_idx == the passed cts_idx always (fib_tracker.py:185-193)
sites.check_to_idx: cts_idx = MarketStructure st.cts.idx. On the raw path (market_structure.py:1716-1724) it is the processing candle; on the pattern path (:1554-1561) it is the CTS anchor, which is <= the apply candle.
sites.as_of_explanation: The snapshot is computed at each CTS refresh and used later. st.poi_inners_for_cycle is read only by _check_proximity_at_candle (market_structure.py:1957), via _maybe_confirm_cts_via_proximity (:643). That path is gated on cts_cycle_id > 0 (:1977) and i > st.cts.idx (:1980). Every st.cts assignment (:1554, :1717, :1723) is followed by a refresh, so the snapshot's cts_idx equals st.cts.idx whenever it is used.
sites.unknowable_reachable: At compute time, yes (an instance with start == cts_idx). It is common: 11/58 H1, 46/280 M15-confluence and 19/122 M15-counter CTS_ESTABLISHED/CTS_UPDATED events have a same-direction instance whose c2 is the event candle. In an instrumented H1 run, 2 of 58 resolver calls would return different inners under c3: sid0 cyc0 cts 163 (3 inners -> []) and cts 171 (2 inners -> []). At decision time, no: the consumption candle i >= cts_idx+1, which is the c3 of any instance in the window, so every counted instance is knowable when it is used. In bounded runs (the Phase-2 probe; the residual at LANDMINES.md:2112-2118), cts == B would need i > B, so the snapshot is never used inside the run.
sites.classification_rationale: The real as-of is the consumption candle, which always comes after the c3 of every instance in the window. A c3 filter keyed to the call's check_to_idx would remove instances that are knowable at every consumption candle until the next refresh, making the result less faithful. H1 showed 0 event delta only because both affected snapshots are cycle 0, which is never consumed. The stale fill as-of (fills between cts and i are ignored) is the separate proposed Plan E stage E3e, not a c3 issue.
sites.r1_vs_r2: At consumption, R1 holds by the bound above. R2 is irrelevant: straddling instances give the correct boolean either way.
sites.effect_if_counted: None when the inners are used. If c3 were wrongly applied here: on H1, 328/328 MarketStructure events and all zone-proximity triggers are unchanged. The M15 exposure is not measured but large (65 events with the imbalance's c2 on the CTS candle, including cycles > 0: confluence sub1 cyc2 at 1940/1942, sub3 cyc1 at 2828/2840, sub7 cyc2 at 4184/4195). It could move CTS_CONFIRMED events confirmed by same-direction zone proximity.
sites.proposed_fix: None. Keep c3 out of this path. If E3e is approved, it should evaluate fills as of the consumption candle; the window still bounds knowability, so E3e does not need c3 either.

notes:
1) THE KEY RESULT, which also answers R1 vs R2 for every boolean consumer. For any has_unfilled_imbalance-style read with as-of t, the only difference from a live engine is instances with start_idx >= t. They overlap the window and count as UNFILLED through the empty-scan branch (types.py:194; imbalance.py:164). Instances with start < t <= end (R1-knowable, R2-not) already give the live answer: the live prefix [start, t-1] exists and is unfilled, and the merged instance also reads unfilled. So R1 (knowable from start_idx+1) is the correct rule, and R2 would be wrong wherever it differs. Evidence: across all 167 H1 and 622 M15 instances, the c2 is never visible at t = start_idx; the prefix is visible and unfilled for every t in [start+1, end+1] (0 violations in 385 + 1464 checks); and min(armed - end) = min(confirmed - end) = 2, so the last c3 never arms its own gap. That last fact follows from the definitions: for a bullish instance gap_top == l[last c3], so stroke 1 cannot fire on that candle (bearish mirrors it).

2) WHERE TO PUT THE RULE (the scoping decision). Fix the POI sweep locally at poi_zones.py:920 (R1); it reproduces exactly last session's 4 measured rows. Do NOT add a c3 filter inside has_unfilled_imbalance without an explicit opt-out: find_ic_candidates would pick it up on both call paths. On the downstream path the as-of is the CTS anchor (0 delta on the window, less faithful in general; Plan E §2.4 item 8). On the in-flight path the result is only used at i > cts. There a wrongly placed filter changes 2 of 58 H1 resolver calls (both cycle 0, never used, so H1 has 0 event delta), but 65 M15 CTS events have an imbalance whose c2 is the CTS candle, including cycles > 0, so MarketStructure events could move on M15 (not measured). Keep is_filled unchanged: 'not knowable yet' is neither filled nor unfilled, and test_imbalance.py:259 pins the empty-scan result. Put knowability in one named accessor (a moment, so the name follows the GLOSSARY Naming Standard — user's call; avoid clashing with the pool's knowable_at_idx) or pass it as an explicit parameter.

3) HOW THIS WAS MEASURED (read-only; no replay run, nothing written in the repo). H1 comes from the baseline save 20260923_172626_0a4eadc, plus in-memory run_pipeline runs on its raw CSV. The base run reproduces all 5 H1 POI histories. Variants: c3 on the in-flight path gave 328/328 identical MarketStructure events and identical proximity triggers; c3 on the downstream path gave identical POIs. M15 uses OHLC decoded from the saved M15 chart HTML: 4228 candles, and the 842 imbalance flags match the chart's two imbalance traces (429 + 413). I used the entity-absolute frame; sub slices recompute imbalances on the slice, which gives the same interior flags. Fib bos/cts come from the M15 fib_lifecycle CSVs, which are absolute.

4) M15 sub7 cyc2 IC 4136 also activates on the c2 of an instance (4195, 4196). R1 leaves it unchanged because the knowable, unfilled instances (4151) and (4174-4176) already satisfy cond3. This is consistent with the measured 4 rows.

5) SYNTHETIC REGRESSION IS READY. Fixture _make_multicycle_data, POI (0,2) IC 12: history is [(15,A)] today and [(15,A),(19,D)] under R1. test_poi_activation_moment.py:157-160 deliberately pins only the first activation, so no existing test fails under R1 (all ran in-process against an R1-patched sweep).

6) STALE DOCS FOUND. IMBALANCE_FILL_SEMANTICS.md:101 calls find_ic_candidates' check_to_idx 'Fib's locked CTS / at Fib lock time'; it is the fib's CTS anchor, and the lock (CTS_CONFIRMED) comes later. sites.unknowable_reachable: YES. The window end == check_to == the CTS anchor A, so an R1-unknowable instance has inst.start_idx == A exactly: c2 is the anchor / new-extreme candle and c3 = A+1 has not closed. It is truly unknowable only when the moment M == A (lag 0); when M > A, c3 <= M has closed and the instance is knowable at the moment. R2-partial instances (start < A <= end) are counted as unfilled via the empty scan, and the live prefix [start, A-1] is also unfilled: its only scan candle is A, a same-direction c2 whose low/high equals the prefix gap edge, so stroke 1 cannot arm. Those are equivalent (except a degenerate prefix with gap <= 0). MEASURED: an R1-unknowable instance was in scope on 4 of 27 calls: M15 sub 1 cyc 2 @1940, sub 2 cyc 0 @2368, sub 3 cyc 1 @2828 (lag 1, so knowable at moment 2829), sub 5 cyc 0 @3656. There was 1 flip: M15 confluence sub 2 cyc 0, EST 2368 (moment 2368, via double_maru). The only sd-direction unfilled instance in [2365, 2368] is (2368, 2368). H1: 0 of 5 calls.
sites.classification_rationale: The one measured flip is a lag-0 row, where anchor == moment, so it is a genuine one-candle lookahead today. The c3 question can be answered correctly now because the moment is on the event (meta['confirmed_at']). Cut on it: count an instance only if inst.start_idx < confirmed_at. Leave the fill horizon at the anchor; moving it is Plan E E3, a separate cause. With this cut, an instance is dropped only when start == A == M, so it is a pure one-cause knowability change. Do NOT key the cut on check_to_idx: on lag>=1 rows that drops a c2==anchor instance that is knowable at the moment. Branch caveat: for the h1 cycle>=1 branches there is no first-activation-on-update path (:1242-1251, :1283-1288), so a fib suppressed here NEVER activates for that cycle. That is the event-granular one-shot asymmetry, and it is a user decision.

sites.plan_e_interaction: PLAN_E_inputs.md §2.4 items 1 and 3 (:652-664): the cts_idx at :521 has two roles. sites.function: FibTracker._update_fib_cts (normal / single branch)
sites.question: After the CTS moves to a new extreme, does the fib's own [BOS, new CTS] still hold an unfilled sd-direction imbalance as of the new CTS candle? That answer drives REACTIVATE (reactivated_at) or DEACTIVATE (reason all_imbalances_filled, deactivated_at) at :1467-1474.
sites.check_to_idx: cts_idx = CTS_UPDATED.idx on every live caller: on_cts_updated → :1169 (cross_cycle cycle-0 fib), :1251 (H1 sid0 cyc≥1), :1288 (H1 sid≥1 plain single), :1327 (H1 Scenario-1 cycle 0), :1590/:1594 (create-on-fail, unreachable for h1), :2525 (cross_failed single extension, anchor_idx == current_candle == CTS_UPDATED.idx from :1218-1227). The :1384 guard lets only a strictly later idx through.
sites.as_of_explanation: Raw-path CTS_UPDATED (via replay_raw) idx = the processed candle = its moment (ARCHITECTURE.md:100). Pattern-path idx = the pattern's extreme candle. That path's apply candle (the moment) is not recorded. When the extreme precedes apply and extends the CTS, a same-idx raw duplicate was processed first and the :1384 guard drops the pattern one. Reference window: 389 raw vs 37 pattern-path CTS_UPDATED rows across the 3 event CSVs. So the as-of is a genuine moment on the raw path.
sites.call_frequency: Once per CTS_UPDATED that reaches an existing unlocked fib (orchestrator.py:203-239 sorted-event loop). Measured 246 calls: H1 2 (via :1288); M15 215 (via :1169) and 29 (via :2525 ← _m15_cross_check:2199 ← _handle_cross_cycle_cts_updated:1218).
sites.unknowable_reachable: yes. The window end equals the as-of, so an R1-unknowable instance means an sd-direction instance with start_idx == cts_idx: the new-extreme candle is itself an FVG c2 (a strong sd candle making the new high/low whose c3 gaps away, the textbook FVG middle). Measured: 41 of 246 calls had one in scope, 0 flips (another knowable unfilled instance was always present).
sites.classification_rationale: On the raw path the as-of is the candle at which the update is knowable, and a c2-at-that-candle FVG needs c3 = cts_idx+1. Counting it is a one-candle lookahead. The pattern path is the parked no-recorded-moment issue; its early-anchor rows are duplicates that the guard drops.
sites.effect_if_counted: Counted as UNFILLED: the fib stays active (an all_imbalances_filled deactivation is suppressed) or reactivates at c2 (reactivated_at = c2). The `active` flag at the last update before CTS_CONFIRMED gates the lock in cross_cycle mode (:1681 single, :1667 cross) and for H1 cycles with a versioned cross (:1754). POI derivation needs locked OR (active AND end_idx None) (poi_zones.py:448), and an unlocked inactive fib vanishes from the chart (export_plotly.py:2538/2547; FIB_LIFECYCLE_SPEC.md:466-470). So a flip can remove a sub fib's lock plus all its POIs. H1 plain singles and sid0 lock unconditionally (:1715-1720, :1762-1770), so for them only active/status and the meta deactivated_at/reactivated_at/reason change. Reference window: 0 flips, 0 delta.

So under c3, an FVG whose c2 is the event candle becomes visible only at the NEXT event, which may never come before the lock. The result can be a lost lock, lost POIs, or a lost fib, not just a one-candle delay. The measured M15 flip shows it: counter sub 5, cyc 1 pre-established check at 3806, with no later re-check. The claim that the c0 lock precedes the cycle-1 EST is strict by mechanism. Cycle 0 can be confirmed only by a pullback, because proximity has a cycle-0 carve-out (market_structure.py:1977). First, 'a central filter does this automatically' has the MS-regression problem described under :1462. Second, the c0 snapshot is consumed only at cycle-1 events (:880 prior_cached_liveness, and here), which are always >= CTS_0+1. Its as-of-CTS_0 inclusion of a c2==CTS_0 instance is therefore a question about retrospective snapshot semantics, not a lookahead. Decide it at :536/:1318 on that basis.

sites.question: Does the pre-established target cycle n+1 have an unfilled sd-direction imbalance in [prospective BOS_{n+1}, current candle] as of the current candle? This decides whether a pre-established cross fib forms or stays active.
sites.check_to_idx: current_candle = int(CTS_THRESHOLD_UPDATED.idx) (fib_tracker.py:2090). The window is [own_imb_start, current_candle], where own_imb_start = _find_prospective_bos = argmin l / argmax h over [cts_n_conf+1, current] (fib_tracker.py:1864-1892, 2102-2105)
sites.as_of_explanation: Verified at the emitter. The ARCHITECTURE table does not cover this event (ARCHITECTURE.md:106 lists *_THRESHOLD_UPDATED as not audited). _emit_cts_threshold_updated(i) is called only from _sync_thresholds_from_range(i) (market_structure.py:1786). Its callers pass the candle MS is processing: _update_active_range(i) at :1257 (from _replay_step_no_patterns(i):624), _ensure_range_on_pullback(apply_idx) at :1343/:1371, the pullback apply at :1601, and the proximity candle at :2157. The orchestrator dispatches the event at that same idx (orchestrator.py:146, 236-239). The anchor and prospective BOS are computed from df.iloc[conf+1 : current+1], so there is no lookahead there.
sites.call_frequency: Once per CTS_THRESHOLD_UPDATED whose target (cycle_id+1) is pre_established. Chain: orchestrator.py:239 -> fib_tracker.py:2061 -> :2107 -> :2158 -> cross_cycle_fib.py:117, and :156 for each walk step. h1 mode returns early at :2075. 46 calls on the reference window, all in M15 sub projections.
sites.unknowable_reachable: YES (R1). The window ends AT t. An sd-direction instance with start_idx == t (c2 = the processing candle, c3 = t+1 not yet closed) overlaps the window, and is_filled's scan (end_idx, t] is empty, so it returns UNFILLED (common/types.py:194, 223-224). An instance with start_idx > t cannot overlap. Measured: 8 of 46 calls had such an instance in scope, and 1 flipped (baseline own_has True, R1 False). The flip is M15.counter sub 5 (first_counter, parent H1 sid 1 cyc 2), sid 0, source cycle 0 -> target cycle 1, THRESHOLD at global 3806 (slice-local 235, 2026-01-13 13:30 UTC), window [3805, 3806]. The only unfilled bullish instance there is (3806,3806), whose c3 is 3807.
sites.classification_rationale: The as-of is a genuine processing candle and the leak is measured on the window. Under R1 the cross never forms: sub 5 has exactly one CTS_THRESHOLD_UPDATED (3806), and cycle 1 is never CTS_ESTABLISHED before the sub ends (4083, same_dir_replacement). No later event re-evaluates the target.
sites.effect_if_counted:
own_has becomes True, the walk runs, and _m15_create_cross v0 fires at t (or an in-place reactivate/extend). That sets activated_at = t, _mark_first_active (the fib start_idx, sticky), _current_cycle[sid] = target, and _obsolete_prev_cycle_all_fibs(end_idx=t), which puts the prior cycles' terminal at t (set-if-absent, irreversible Option-A early end). POIs are then derived from the cross fib. The same leak can also block a legitimate own_imb_filled deactivation.

sites.r1_vs_r2: R1 is enough. A merged run that straddles t (start < t <= end) is counted unfilled either way: its live partial [start, t-1] (c3 = t) overlaps the window whenever own_imb_start <= t-1, and its scan covers only c3, which cannot arm stroke 1. R2 differs only in two corners: (a) own_imb_start == t, which needs an outside bar that is both the lowest low since the confirmation and a new range high (for an sd run, t <= conf+2); (b) a degenerate partial gap. sites.plan_e_interaction: No as-of conflict: the THRESHOLD idx is a moment, and this site is not in Plan E's timing list. This fix also removes the only instance on this window of the parked fallback-POI item.
sites.proposed_fix:
Count an instance only if inst.start_idx + 1 <= current_candle. Thread it as a knowable_at parameter (resolve_cross_cycle_eligibility -> has_unfilled_imbalance, default = check_to_idx) rather than changing the has_unfilled_imbalance default that other groups share.

DESIGN QUESTION: FibTracker is event-driven, so under c3 the cross forms at the NEXT evaluation event, or never (as here), not at c3 = t+1. The POI sweep is per-candle, which is why it shifted by exactly 1. If you want one-candle-later semantics, the c3 candle of an in-window sd-instance must become an evaluation trigger; that would keep sub 5's cross (born 3807) and the fallback POI row.

notes:
1. How this was measured (all read-only; nothing written in the repo, git status stayed clean)
   - Ran in-memory `run_pipeline(raw H1 CSV from save 20260923_172626_0a4eadc, lower_timeframes=("M15",))` with the M15 data fetched from OANDA. The baseline exports reproduced the saved CSVs byte-identically (H1 and both lenses: POI, fib, KL and events tables).
   - Recorded all 307 G4 imbalance reads through a monkeypatch of `cross_cycle_fib.has_unfilled_imbalance`, evaluating the baseline, R1 and R2 answers side by side.
   - Scripts and outputs are in the scratchpad: `g4_h1_probe.py`, `g4_recs_M15.json`, `g4_variant_run.py`, `out_base2/`, `out_r1b/`, `g4r1plugin.py`.

2. Measured footprint of R1 at every G4 site (all callers, including the MS in-flight resolver)
   - Exactly one flip, at `on_cts_threshold_updated`: M15.counter sub 5, THRESHOLD event at global 3806.
   - 2 of the 24 CSVs change: `M15_counter_fib_lifecycle` 9→8 rows and `M15_counter_poi_zones` 13→12 rows.
   - Unchanged: every H1 table, every confluence table, and the counter KL/events/WVMI tables. The subs/triggers/unresolved tables are also identical.
   - The removed POI is the parked "never-established-cycle fallback POI" (sub 5 cyc 1 IC 3654). Its only instance on this window was born from a gap that was not yet knowable.
   - R2 adds no further flips.

3. Design point: event-driven sites vs the per-candle POI sweep
   - FibTracker evaluates only at structure events. Under the c3 rule, a cross that leaked at c2 forms at the next event, or never; it does not form at c3.
   - That is why the POI sweep moved by one candle while sub 5's cross vanishes entirely.
   - If you want "one candle later" semantics, the c3 candle of an in-window sd-instance has to become an evaluation trigger.

4. Consumption-moment principle: judge knowability where a value is USED, not where it is computed
   - Three G4-adjacent values are consumed only after c3 has closed: the MS in-flight POI inners (gated on `i > st.cts.idx`, `market_structure.py:1980`), the snapshot cond3 at `:149`, and the cached cond2 `c0['has_unfilled']`.
   - A blanket `start_idx < check_to_idx` filter inside `has_unfilled_imbalance` would over-correct all three.
   - Recommendation: add an explicit per-caller `knowable_at` parameter:
     - THRESHOLD and raw-UPDATED callers: `knowable_at = current_candle`.
     - EST callers: `confirmed_at`, or defer to Plan E E3a.
     - Pattern-path UPDATED: none until its moment is recorded.
     - MS in-flight: `st.cts.idx + 1`, or none.

1) KEY ANSWER to (b), look-ahead. Every in-flight window ends at cts <= P, and cts == P on the raw path. So an instance with c2 == P == cts IS counted at computation time: its c3 = P+1 has not closed yet, and is_filled's empty scan (types.py:194, 223-224) counts it as unfilled. c2 > P is impossible. The snapshot is only CONSUMED at i > st.cts.idx (proximity gate market_structure.py:1980) or at a later cycle-1 refresh, and by then c3 has closed. So this is a refresh-cadence leak (a live engine that refreshes only at CTS events would not have the FVG until its next refresh). It is NOT a decision-time look-ahead.

2) MEASURED on the reference window, both cutoffs: 0 changes to H1 events, M15 events / KL / POI / subs on either lens. There were 459 (moment) / 461 (anchor) flipped reads (455 find_ic at P==cts; 4 cycle-0 snapshot; 0 cross_cycle). Only 4 refresh snapshots changed, and all were sid-0 cycle-0, which is unconsumed by construction. The anchor cutoff's 2 extra exclusions (M15 slice-local cts 239, P 240 = the lag-1 EST sub 3 cyc 1) drop an FVG that is already knowable at P. That is concrete evidence that an anchor-relative c3 rule is less faithful and belongs with Plan E E3e.

3) Scope recommendation for the MS group: no MS engine change in the c3 commit. The MS sites are defer_to_plan_e (E3e + §2.4 items 2, 5, 8, 9). If the POI/fib groups add a c3 rule inside has_unfilled_imbalance or find_ic_candidates, the MS in-flight path inherits it automatically. The predicted MS-side delta is 0 on this window (measured). Parity: the MS cycle-0 snapshot must change in the same commit as FibTracker's c0 snapshot (fib_tracker.py:536, :1318) or the Scenario-2 anchor agreement breaks (LANDMINES:188-223).

4) Consumption scope. cycle0_data is consumed only in H1 main sid>=1 cycle-1 runs. Subs and probes run structure_id=0 (structure_engine.py:893, unified_probe.py:537), so select_fib_anchor_for_cycle always returns 'intra' for them. After any _rewind_to in an H1 sid>=1 run, state.structure_id resets to 0 (market_structure.py:560; known in LANDMINES:1187-1194), which would silently disable the in-flight Scenario-2 for the rest of that run.

5) The Plan A imbalance residual (LANDMINES:2112-2119) is unobservable in bounded MS outputs by the same consumption-time bound. start>=B instances are counted only at cts==P==B and consumed only past B. Straddlers are boolean-equivalent. The only theoretical hole is a degenerate merged gap: types.py:196-197 treats gap<=0 as filled, and a merged run can be degenerate while its prefix is valid (possible geometry: h[s]<h[s-1] and a gap-up c3). There are 0 such runs on this window (H1 167 / M15 622 instances; 0 degenerate; 0 prefix-validity flips). verdicts.refutation: The as_of_kind (mixed) and the reachability (YES for R1, only start_idx == cts_0 == P) both hold. I re-ran g5_h1_ms.py and it reproduces the H1 flips at cts 163 and 171 in both modes, with the 328 events unchanged. The defer classification does not hold, for three reasons. (1) 'Knowable at consumption, so an anchor cutoff is LESS faithful' mixes up when the bit is used with what the bit means. The value is a cache written at the refresh candle P (:2001-2002). A locked snapshot is never recomputed (:2038-2039, locked at :1892-1893), and it is defined as 'unfilled as of cts_idx' (:2027-2028; CROSS_CYCLE_FIB_SPEC.md:163 'frozen snapshots'). At P, a live run of the same code cannot flag c2 == P, because compute_imbalance needs row P+1 (imbalance.py:55-67). The live cached cond2 therefore never contains that FVG, so this leak lasts through every cycle-1 consumption; it is not a cadence artifact. In the only reachable case the anchor cutoff and the moment cutoff are the same cutoff, so the anchor cutoff is exactly faithful there. (2) Plan E does not close it. E3 moves anchors to moments, and on the raw path the moment is cts itself, so the reachable case is untouched. R1 would 'hold automatically' only if E3 made cond2's as-of CTS_0 CONFIRMED, which PLAN_E_inputs §2.4 item 5 leaves undecided. The claim that 'E3e would have to undo it' is also wrong: a rule relative to check_to composes with any later move of the as-of. (3) Parity does not force deferral. FibTracker's c0 checks use the same check_to, the CTS_0 idx (fib_tracker.py:536-538, :1318-1321, :1436-1438, :1527-1530). A rule inside has_unfilled_imbalance therefore moves MS and FibTracker together; only a P-relative cutoff could not be mirrored. The residual that does belong to Plan E: on pattern-path lag (cts_0 < P) a check_to-relative rule over-excludes c2 == cts_0, whose c3 is at or before P. Predicted consumed delta on this window: 0.

An sd trigger can therefore vanish, move later, or be relabelled POI->BOS, but can never fire earlier. notes:
1) How the fix propagates: POI activation_history reaches engine decisions through exactly one path. H1 zone_proximity (zone_proximity.py:487) feeds (a) the WVMI gate (orchestrator.py:344-364), which feeds UC1 first_counter; (b) subsequent_confluence/counter triggers; (c) the sub-WVMI streams. All three feed the lifecycle sweep and the M15 subs. Subs never run zone proximity (pooled_structure_build.py:89 skip_wvmi=True), so M15 POI activation changes show only in CSVs and charts. No G6 site reads an imbalance c2 idx as a TIME on its own. The only independent imbalance-idx reads are rendering the pattern location (is_imbalance highlight, out_of_scope) and exports (write_only).

2) Monotonicity, usable as a prediction criterion: c3 (R1) and last-c3 (R2) only delay the sweep's enter. Existing guards only drop instances, and leave events are unchanged. So POI activity can only shrink, and proximity sd triggers can only vanish, move later, or relabel POI->BOS. Downstream deltas are limited to cycles where a base sd trigger falls on a candle whose POI activity is removed.

3) Measured, read-only: I ran the H1 pipeline in memory on the saved 0a4eadc raw CSV with lower_timeframes=(); the baseline POI histories reproduce exactly. With only the POI sweep enter patched in memory:

Note that test_imbalance.py:259 test_is_filled_empty_scan_range pins the primitive's 'unknowable counts as unfilled' behaviour (primary group).

If the fib group applies c3 against its ANCHOR as-of, then any unlocked fib whose only unfilled sd instance has c2 at or after the CTS anchor goes inactive, and ALL of its POIs vanish (a row-level delta, not a 1-candle shift). verdicts.refutation: The monotonicity proof is wrong in general, and the reader offers it as a prediction criterion. Rule 3's narrow caps (zone_proximity.py:390-391 init, :422-425 skip, :450-454 set) are per-cycle latches that never reset. Suppose the base fires an sd:POI trigger in narrow mode on a c2 candle, which sets narrow_sd_fired. The fixed run does not fire there, so the flag stays False. If the next sd trigger then fires in non-narrow mode, a later narrow-mode sd candle that the base BLOCKED can now fire. So after the first divergence a trigger can move EARLIER or be ADDED, and new var3/var4 pairs and M15 subs are possible. 'Vanish, move later, or relabel POI->BOS, never earlier' does not hold. The precondition is correct: new sd qualification is a subset of base per candle and the state machine is identical up to the first divergence. So a delta requires a base sd trigger on a candle whose POI activity is removed. The label 'equivalent' is acceptable only in the sense of no own code change. The output is NOT invariant: at 997 the site did evaluate a POI whose only entering sd instance (997-999) was unknowable. It must be in the prediction set and pinned by a new red-first test. I confirmed analytically that the reference window is invariant: 953 falls under expected opp_sd (926 sd -> 954 opp_sd). 997-999 fall under expected sd with no base trigger even with the POI active, so removing an inner cannot create one. The flags and the sequence are identical under R1 and R2.
verdicts.extra_findings: R2 over-excludes for this existence question. The partial FVG at 997 is knowable at 998, which is its c3 (instance 997-999 in the baseline _imbalance_instances.csv), but R2 keeps the POI inactive until 1000. R1 is the faithful enter for cond3. The poi_active_as_of end-of-candle vs start-of-candle point (GOTCHAS narrow-gap rule) is valid and pre-existing.

sites.classification_rationale: Needs a new section (the commit's promised c3 rule). One canonical home here; every other doc cross-links in one line. Proposed wording: (1) An instance is knowable as of candle t iff inst.start_idx + 1 <= t (its first c3 has closed) - rule R1. Consumers exclude start_idx >= check_to_idx BEFORE the fill check; the POI sweep enters at max(inst.start_idx + 1, first_active). (2) While start_idx < t <= end_idx the run is still growing. Its knowable part [start_idx, t-1] is unfilled at t whatever its bounds: its only post-run candle is its own c3, and c3 cannot arm stroke 1 (bullish l[c3] == gap_top > gap_top - 0.7*gap_size; bearish mirrored). This needs fill_threshold > 0. So counting the retro-merged instance as unfilled is exact, and the merged-bounds hindsight cannot change the boolean. Bounds are final from end_idx+1, before any fill can be confirmed. (3) Do NOT use end_idx+1 (R2): it is over-strict and drops a growing run that a live engine sees. Measured: wrapper-R2 fails 10 tests (see the test records). (4) check_to_idx must be a MOMENT. A site whose as-of is still an anchor (Plan E E3) applies the rule against the anchor. That is exact when anchor == moment, and over-strict when anchor < moment by exactly one instance: the one whose c2 == the anchor. (5) Overlap: the knowable extent is [start, min(end, t-1)]. Using inst.overlaps on the full [start,end] is equivalent for every current call shape: window start < t, or the candle before window start is a -sd IC, which cannot be a c2 of an sd run. (6) is_filled keeps its empty-scan False. Knowability is a separate predicate.

CONSEQUENCES:
(1) No existing test pins either leak (the enter-at-c2 sweep, or the wrapper counting start_idx >= check_to_idx). Tests-first needs new pins. Ready-made failing-first fixture: _make_multicycle_data POI (0,2) IC 12. Its full history is [(15,T)] today and [(15,T),(19,F,imbalance_filled)] under sweep-R1: at 19, instance (14,14) leaves (confirmed_fill_idx 19) and (19,22) would enter at 20 > scan_end 19. PLAN_D:158 anticipated this.
(2) R1 (start_idx+1 <= t) is EXACT for the unfilled boolean, and R2 is over-strict. Proof: a growing run's knowable part [start, t-1] is unfilled at t whatever its bounds, because its only post-run candle is its own c3, which cannot arm stroke 1: bullish l[c3] == gap_top > gap_top - 0.7*gap_size. Bounds are final from end_idx+1, before any fill. So GOTCHAS 'merged hindsight bias' is benign for the boolean. CAVEAT: the proof needs fill_threshold > 0. With 0, c3 would arm and confirm on itself; no config uses 0, but a guard or a note is worth adding.
(3) R1 in the wrapper also closes the existence half of the Plan A attrs['imbalances'] residual (LANDMINES:2112-2119, MARKET_STRUCTURE_SPEC:329-332). With it, has_unfilled_imbalance is equal on bounded and truncated frames at every as-of <= B.
(4) In the test suite, unknowable instances reach ONLY the MS in-flight path: 333 R1 flips at market_structure.py:2050 and poi_zones.py:229 via compute_poi_inners_for_cycle, all in test_ms_bounded_equals_truncated. Fib, cross-cycle and derive_poi_zones sites have zero coverage.
(5) Scope argument from the docs: ARCHITECTURE.md:217 and poi_zones.py:516 DEFINE the sweep as has_unfilled_imbalance(df, ic_idx+1, t, check_to_idx=t, direction=sd), and that identity holds today (verified). Sweep-only breaks it; wrapper + sweep together preserves it.
(6) Anchor as-of sites (fib_tracker :536/:1183/:1318/:1436-1571, MS :2050, find_ic_candidates :229): c3 applied against the anchor is exact when anchor == moment (all 5 H1 cycles; 31/34 EST rows). When anchor < moment it is over-strict by exactly the instance whose c2 == the anchor. cond3 (window [BOS_0,CTS_0], as-of BOS_1 > CTS_0) and the prior-cycle walks are geometrically bounded.
(7) CROSS_CYCLE_FIB_SPEC:165-166's '{B creates cross} => {A creates cross}' relies on unfilled being monotone in the as-of. Under the c3 rule the knowable set grows with the as-of, so the claim can fail when c2 == CTS_0. Qualify it, and measure before predicting.

sites.classification_rationale: This is the only path by which the knowability defect changes MarketStructure EVENTS (structure itself), and no group listed it as a site. It has no own read; its input comes from the G5 producer sites, whose as-of is the CTS anchor. On raw-path refreshes the anchor equals the moment, so c3 measured against check_to_idx is correct there. On pattern-path refreshes (apply_idx > anchor possible), measuring against the anchor over-excludes: an instance with start_idx == anchor has c3 = anchor+1 <= apply_idx and is knowable. A correct fix needs the (moment, anchor) split, which is PLAN_E E3e (only PROPOSED, Q4.18). Second interaction: the snapshot only refreshes at CTS events (MARKET_STRUCTURE_SPEC.md:203-212). A c3 exclusion at a raw refresh therefore persists until the next new extreme; if price pulls back from i, the instance whose c3 = i+1 is never added. That permanently removes a POI inner for the cycle, which matches the spec'd snapshot engine but is a behavior change the plan must predict.
sites.effect_if_counted: An extra POI inner closer to price (max for sd=+1, min for sd=-1; :122-131) produces an earlier or different sd-prox CTS_CONFIRMED. That moves RANGE_STARTED (proximity_created_range), cts_threshold, and the BOS_{n+1} window [cts_confirmed_idx, breakout] (:2236-2238), so BOS/CTS events move. The cascade reaches KL CTS zone confirmed_idx / confirmation_method, fib lock, POI end, zone_proximity triggers, sub triggers and the pool, and WVMI. It also reaches the unified_probe Phase-2 CTS count (stop_after_cts_established=2).
sites.r1_vs_r2: Matters. 2 of the 4 measured H1 differences are R2-only (pattern@172 inst 171-172, pattern@703 inst 702-703: second c2 == refresh moment). R1 keeps them with their final merged bounds; R2 drops them.
sites.plan_e_interaction: E3e (MS in-flight POI-inner resolver evaluates as-of the CTS anchor; ARCHITECTURE.md:136-142). Applying c3 against cts_idx now is correct for raw-path refreshes but wrong-direction for pattern-path refreshes.

verdicts.corrected_as_of_kind: moment. The decision reads the snapshot only at a processing candle i > st.cts.idx (market_structure.py:1980). The snapshot's internal fill as-of is the CTS anchor, which is the separate E3e fill-timing item and says nothing about existence.
verdicts.refutation:
The measurement is real, but it tests the wrong candle. The reader applied c3 at the REFRESH candle. Nothing makes a decision there.

(1) The only reader of st.poi_inners_for_cycle is _check_proximity_at_candle (:1957; grep finds no other reader). It is gated by `i > st.cts.idx` (:1980). Every live st.cts assignment is followed by a refresh (:1554->:1561, :1717->:1718, :1723->:1724), so the snapshot's cts_idx always equals st.cts.idx.

(2) Every window that feeds the snapshot ends at or before that cts_idx:
- find_ic_candidates: range(bos_idx, cts_idx+1) and cond3 end_idx=cts_idx (poi_zones.py:220, :229-236).
- cond1 over [BOS_1, CTS_1] (fib_tracker.py:169-176 -> cross_cycle_fib.py:117-121).
- cond3 and c0 over [BOS_0, CTS_0] (cross_cycle_fib.py:146-152, market_structure.py:2044-2052).
So every admitted instance has start_idx <= cts_idx <= i-1. Its first c3 has therefore closed at every candle where the snapshot is read. Under R1 no unknowable instance can reach a CTS_CONFIRMED, RANGE_STARTED or BOS decision. This also covers M15.confluence @1902 (anchor 1898), without needing M15 data.

(3) "On raw-path refreshes the anchor equals the moment, so c3 against check_to_idx is correct there" is wrong. The snapshot is never read at the refresh candle (:1980). A filter there would drop the c2=i instance, which is knowable at i+1. Because refreshes happen only on a new CTS extreme (MARKET_STRUCTURE_SPEC.md:203-208), it would stay dropped until the next extreme. That is a new divergence from the per-candle check the spec says this snapshot approximates. The proposed fix (thread the refresh moment through the resolver) has the same defect.

(4) R2 is not the live-faithful rule here. Take a candle i with cts_idx < i <= end. The live prefix instance [start, min(end, i-1)] gives the same boolean as the merged instance:
- Overlap: every window ends at or before cts_idx, and the prefix already covers every c2 up to cts_idx.
- Fill: check_to_idx is cts_idx. If the prefix end is >= cts_idx, both scans are empty (types.py:216-224). Otherwise the prefix and merged instances are the same object.
So the 2 R2-only diffs (@172, @703) are over-exclusions.

(5) E3e (ARCHITECTURE.md:140-141, PLAN_E_inputs.md:638) is about the FILL as-of, not existence. Even under a refresh-time rule, the moment is already in MS state (i on the raw path; apply_idx set at :1556 before the refresh at :1561). So none of this is blocked on Plan E.
verdicts.extra_findings:
- Exception to (4): is_filled returns True for gap_size<=0 before it reaches the empty-range branch (types.py:195-196). So a degenerate merged run built with a future c3 reads as FILLED where the live prefix would read unfilled. The H1 baseline has 0 of 167 such instances (instances CSV gap_size). M15 is unverified.
- Parity: MS :2050 and select_fib_anchor_for_cycle intentionally mirror FibTracker (market_structure.py:68-80). FibTracker :1318 has an IMMEDIATE consumer at the same event (:1330, :1351 Scenario-1 activation at activated_at=cts_idx); MS has none. A c3 rule applied to FibTracker's cycle-0 snapshot must not be copied blindly into MS :2050, and the MS<->FibTracker parity claim needs restating either way.
- Doc action: record this bound in the MS spec snapshot paragraph, so nobody adds a refresh-time c3 filter.

- The call-site list has 16 entries, not 15: MS 1, cross 3, fib 11, poi 1.
- fib :1436 and :1527 (cond1 as-of c0_cts_idx) also have end_idx == check_to_idx but were left out of the reachable list.
- The rationale holds, and more strongly than stated. Keying knowability to check_to_idx is wrong even where anchor == refresh moment (the MS raw path; see the MS verdict: its snapshot is read only at i > cts_idx). It also stays wrong after Plan E for deliberately historical as-of questions. The docstring itself names one (imbalance.py:147-149, 'did BOS_1 fill cycle 0's imbalances' as-of BOS_1). Fill-as-of and knowable-at are permanently separate parameters, which supports the opt-in knowable_at_idx proposal. Only making it the default is deferred; the parameter itself needs no Plan E.
- The claim 'the difference is existence only' has two caveats:
  (a) The degenerate-gap branch (types.py:195-196) returns filled from future-derived merged bounds.
  (b) R1 as written (start_idx+1 <= t, overlap over the full merged span) can admit a run through a not-yet-knowable later c2 when the caller's window starts inside the run. The exact rule is to test overlap against [start, min(end, t-1)]. This cannot happen for IC cond3: cand has direction -sd and cannot sit inside an sd run, because c2 direction must match (imbalance.py:59-64).

Verified:
- activated_at, _set_terminal set-if-absent (:334-336), _mark_first_active setdefault (:319), and the cycle pass-through fed as an earliest-wins candidate (:427-429).
- Baseline exposure: H1 1/3 rows new_cycle (sid1 cyc1 end 902), confluence 13/21, counter 5/9.
- POI gate at poi_zones.py:448.

Corrections:
- The activated_at list omits :602, :865 and :1200, which also use cts_idx.
- 'current_candle for cross_cycle creations' is mostly an anchor too: callers pass current_candle=cts_idx at :614, :1223 and :1968. Only the THRESHOLD path (:2092 current_candle=event.idx -> :2112) is a genuine moment. So the written start/end timestamps are anchors on nearly every path, which strengthens the Plan E E3 classification.

- The bound holds. cts_by_cycle is filled only at CTS_CONFIRMED with the cts_anchor_idx value (fib_tracker.py:1640-1642). Every step-2 window ends at CTS_k (cross_cycle_fib.py:146-147), and every as-of is later than that:
  - EST/UPDATED: current_candle = CTS_target anchor.
  - THRESHOLD: event.idx, which is at or after the CTS_n confirmation.
  - snapshot: own_imb_start = BOS_{k+1}, whose window starts at the pullback apply or cts_confirmed_idx (market_structure.py:2234-2238).
- The 'same-candle corner' looks unreachable. A pullback CTS_CONFIRMED at apply_idx follows a back-fill of only [i, apply_idx) (:1004-1008). Raw CTS updates stop once CONFIRMED (:1710-1711). So st.cts.idx < apply_idx at pullback confirmation, and sd-prox confirmation needs i > cts.idx (:1980).
- The R2 latch caveat is correct and important: under R2 a cycle would be judged dead and latched permanently (:160-162).

get_unfilled_imbalances (imbalance.py:169-183) is equally dead in production: it is imported at fib_tracker.py:25 but never called, and appears only in tests (test_imbalance.py:343). It is documented in IMBALANCE_FILL_SEMANTICS.md:83 and LANDMINES.md:1516 as a deferred use. Document it the same way (no existence as-of) in the new knowability section.
